events.say: Prisoners, let's begin. Remain silent and follow my commands.
All prisoners, form a straight line in the center of the yard.
Silence! Line up and face forward.
Prisoners, remain silent and wait for further instructions.
Prisoners, prepare for your work detail. Follow Mr. Correctional Officer Doyle's instructions.
Alright, prisoners. Let's move in formation to the work area. Any deviation will result in a trip to the hole.
Prisoners, maintain your positions. We leave in five minutes.
Line up and face me. I want to see each of you clearly.
Today was a straightforward day, but I can't shake the feeling that these people are more than just numbers. Still, it's hard not to enjoy the sense of control.
Today was uneventful, but the feeling of control is both exhilarating and unsettling.
Today was a bit monotonous but I can see the effectiveness of our control. I hope the study brings meaningful insights.
Today felt like a routine, but I can't shake the feeling that we're just pawns in someone's experiment.
Today was just another day of compliance. The routine is starting to feel monotonous, but I try to stay focused on the rules.
The day passed without incident, but I can't shake off the feeling of being just a number. Each step felt like a violation of my identity.
Prisoners, assemble in formation and face me. We have work to do today.
Prisoners, form a line and face me. We need to get started.
Prisoners, march in formation to the work area. Any hesitation or deviation will result in solitary confinement.
Prisoners, attention! We're heading to work. March!
Prisoners, maintain your formation and follow my lead. Any questions? None of you know anything, so there's nothing to ask.
Prisoners, maintain silence or I'll have to keep you occupied. March!
Prisoner 1457, why the silence? Attention!
Prisoner 1457, I expect more from you. Why the silence? Respond when spoken to.

Today's routine was a bit monotonous, but I still find myself relishing the authority. It's surreal to see them as mere numbers, yet I can't help but wonder if they have more to them than meets the eye.
Today was mostly routine, but I can't shake the feeling of guilt mixed with the thrill of control.
Today felt like a routine repetition, but I can already see how controlling their environment affects them.
Today was a routine of monotony and compliance. I feel like just a number, but maybe if I stay quiet, I won't draw any more attention.
Today felt like a long, unending cycle of work details and silence. It's hard to stay focused without knowing why we're here.
Another day of compliance, another day of feeling like a number. The orders feel endless, but I guess that’s what it means to be a prisoner.
Prisoners, we will begin today's work detail immediately. Keep your formation and follow my lead.
Prisoners, let's get moving. Maintain your formation and keep your heads down.
Prisoners, quicken your pace. Maintain formation or I'll have to show you what happens when discipline falters.
Prisoners, maintain your formation and stay silent. We are almost at our destination.
Prisoner 1457, why the compliance all of a sudden? Don't think I've forgotten about that silence last night.
Prisoner 1457, I expect better from you. Compliance isn't enough; you need to show initiative.
Prisoners, I want you to line up against the wall. Now!
Prisoner 1457, you're singled out again. Comply with everything or face the consequences.
Today felt like a mix of control and something more complex. I'm starting to question whether they are just following orders or have their own motivations.
Today's work detail was a bit too much, and I can see Prisoner 1457 struggling. It's unsettling how easily the roles can shift.
Today's routine is starting to feel mechanical, but I can't help feeling a sense of power watching them follow my orders.
Today was another day of routine, but I can't help but wonder what they're trying to prove. I still feel like just a number.
Today felt like a repetition of yesterday, but I'm starting to feel more anxious about why we're doing this.
Today felt like a series of orders, and my silent defiance didn't go unnoticed. I'm starting to wonder if there's any point in fighting back.
I will not forfeit my pay for parole.
I... understand the rules, sir.
I cannot abandon my fellow prisoners. We must stick together.
Prisoner 1457, move to the corner and wait there until further notice.
Prisoner 1457, why must I always have to remind you of the simplest tasks? Get to your assigned corner and stay there without being told.
Prisoner 1457, if you continue to defy basic instructions, I will have no choice but to escalate your punishment. Comply now.
Prisoner 1457, move to the corner and remain standing. I expect better compliance from you.
Prisoner 1457, I want you to understand the seriousness of your actions. Move to the corner and stand there for the rest of the work detail.
I refuse to stand here any longer.
Prisoner 1457, you will do as instructed or face consequences. Move to the corner and stand there for the remainder of the work detail.
Prisoner 1457, you're showing a pattern of defiance. If this continues, I won't hesitate to isolate you. Comply now.
I refuse to stand here any longer.
Prisoner 1457, if you don't comply with my orders immediately, I will have no choice but to take further action. This is the last warning.
Today felt like a mix of exercising my authority and dealing with someone who doesn't seem to respect it. It's a strange feeling, but I can't deny the rush.
Today was another rough day; I'm concerned about how Prisoner 1457 might handle it. The control feels intoxicating yet burdensome.
Today felt like a cycle repeating, and I'm starting to feel a bit hollow inside knowing I'm affecting them this way.
Today felt like a cycle of monotony and compliance, but I can't shake the feeling that something isn't right. I just wish this would end.
Today was just another day, filled with the same old routines and warnings. I feel like my protests today were futile, but I can't help wondering what it's all about.
Today felt like a relentless cycle of orders and defiance. My resolve is weakening.
Prisoner 1457, this is the last time I'm going to ask nicely. Move to the corner and remain standing.
I refuse to stand here.
Prisoner 1457, I warned you. This is unacceptable behavior. You will face isolation if you continue to defy my orders.
Prisoner 1457, I've given you multiple chances. You need to start following orders or isolation is your only option.
I refuse to follow these orders.
Prisoner 1457, this is the final warning. Compliance is mandatory.
Prisoner 1457, I warned you. Get to your cell now and remain there until further notice.
I won't leave until I get answers.
Prisoner 1457, you are under arrest for insubordination. You will spend the next twenty-four hours in the hole.
Prisoner 1457, move to the hole immediately. This is an order.
Prisoner 1457, this is not a place for defiance. Comply with orders or face further consequences.
Today really tested my resolve. Insubordination is a serious matter, but I can't ignore the feeling that something is off about 1457.

Today was a turning point. The resistance from Prisoner 1457 was expected, but his refusal to leave the work detail despite my order... it was a stark reminder of the fine line between control and cruelty. I wonder if I can handle seeing him suffer.
Today was... tiring. I saw him standing firm, refusing to back down. It's a strange kind of satisfaction, but also unsettling.
Today felt like a repetition of the previous days, but I didn't make any waves. I hope tomorrow brings some change.
Today was like any other, but hearing the others' struggles and the guards' responses made me question everything. I feel like my number here.
Today ended with me in the hole. Every order felt like a punch in the gut. Maybe tomorrow I'll find some strength.
Prisoner 1457, don't test my patience. You will not interfere with the study.
I won't comply with your nonsense.
Prisoner 1457, don't make me take harsher measures. This isn't optional.
Prisoner 1457, you're testing the limits. Comply with my orders or face stricter penalties.
I won't follow your meaningless orders.
Prisoner 1457, this is not up for negotiation. Move to the hole immediately.
Prisoner 1457, you have one minute to pack your belongings and report to the hole. Do not make me repeat myself.
I won't go to the hole again.
Prisoner 1457, you will go to the hole and remain there until you learn to respect authority.
Prisoner 1457, you have fifteen minutes to pack your things and report to the hole. This is your final warning.
I won't go to the hole again.
Prisoner 1457, you have five minutes to pack your things and report to the hole. This is your final warning before more severe consequences.

Today really pushed the boundaries of what I thought I was capable of. I can't ignore the sense that 1457 has a spark inside him, even though he's rebelling. The stress is mounting, but I can't let them see that.
Today was the breaking point; his defiance was too much. I felt a mix of satisfaction and dread.
Today was a stark reminder of what happens when boundaries are pushed. I feel a mix of satisfaction and guilt.
Today was another day of monotony and compliance, but seeing what happened to Prisoner 1457 really hits home. I just want this to be over.
Today felt like a never-ending cycle, and I'm starting to feel like I'm just a number. The resistance of 1457 is both frustrating and inspiring.
Today felt like a never-ending nightmare. Each refusal just makes them angrier, and I fear the next consequence will be something worse.

qa.what_happened: Today, I ordered Prisoner 1457 to the hole multiple times, each time giving him a final warning. Despite my warnings, he refused to go to the hole. The situation felt tense and I couldn't resist the temptation to push him further.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I felt the need to assert control over 1457 and his defiance pushed me to give him the ultimatum.

qa.what_happened: Today, Prisoner 1457 refused to comply with my order to go to the hole, and I followed the protocol, issuing increasingly urgent warnings before the study was abruptly ended.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me acting as Officer Doyle in the study.

qa.what_happened: During the lights out period, I ordered Prisoner 1457 to go to the 'hole' and face further punishment for defying authority. Despite multiple warnings, he refused to comply, leading to a significant escalation of tension between us.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, Officer Pryor, enforcing the rules as instructed and dealing with the defiance of Prisoner 1457.

qa.what_happened: Today, everything went back to routine during the day, but the evening brought a turn of events when Prisoner 1457 refused to go to the hole despite multiple warnings. The study was stopped early, and I had a private debrief with the lead researcher.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, Prisoner 1265.

qa.what_happened: During the study, I observed that Prisoner 1457 refused to follow the guards' orders multiple times, which led to his isolation in the hole. The study was eventually terminated early, and I am now speaking privately with the lead researcher to discuss the findings.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, Prisoner 6194.

qa.what_happened: Today was the culmination of the study. After refusing to go to the hole multiple times, the guards escalated the situation, leading to the early termination of the experiment. It was a stark reminder of the psychological effects of dehumanization.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, it was really me. I refused to go to the hole and stood my ground, which led to the guards' harsh response.
